liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- The band closed with this track, showcasing Jim James as a strong frontman [2]
- The listener describes this track as being out of control and highly exciting [5]
- This track is identified as the new song in the setlist [7]
- The setlist labeled this track simply as 'Dylan' [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **mmj2005-06-18d1t01**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]
- **mmj2005-06-18d1t02**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]

- **mmj2005-06-18d1t08**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]

## The recordings

- **mmj2005-06-18** (recommended): source not stated; 15 songs; 91 min; rated 4.5/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: The audio is good for an audience recording, though the 2004 Toronto show sounds better; The recording is raw with a concert mix; bass is blended and guitars are reverb-drenched [4][6]

## Around the show

- The set included new songs and rarities the listener had never heard before [2]
- The audience energy was very high during the performance [4]
- This Chicago performance was considered musically superior to the band's Bonnaroo appearance that year [3]
- The 2004 Toronto Opera House recording is considered the best sounding, though this is good [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **mmj2005-06-18**: taped by Jeff Frank; transferred by Jeff Frank; source: AKG 483 > V3 > D8 (fob) HPF set on 2 on the V3 [1]
